# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 5 (Bu-Vb Np5)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Np5
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 5
**Title (English, from literature):** Receiving a robe from a nun
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 5, titled *Cīvarapaṭiggahana* ("Receiving a robe from a nun"), stipulates that a Buddhist monk who accepts robe-cloth from a nun must relinquish the cloth and confess the offense. In the narrative framing accompanying the rule in the Pāli Vinaya, the Venerable Udāyin—a monk whose misbehavior frequently prompts the promulgation of monastic regulations—is described as having been left behind as a monastery caretaker (*āyasmā udāyi ohiyyako hoti vihārapālo*), an assignment that Jonathan Silk observes was likely no mark of honor in this monastic context [Silk 2008].
